text: Tell me about a time you failed or made a significant mistake. What did you learn, and what did you change afterwards?
assesses: Growth mindset: owning mistakes, reflecting honestly and turning lessons into lasting changes.
strongSignals: Picks a real failure with real consequences
Takes clear personal ownership without blaming others
Explains the root cause, not just the symptom
Describes concrete changes (process, tests, habits) that stuck
redFlags: A 'failure' that is really a disguised strength
followUps: What would you do differently on day one?
How did you tell stakeholders?
Has that lesson helped you since?

text: Describe a time you had to learn a new technology or domain quickly to deliver something important.
assesses: Learn-it-all attitude, how you get up to speed and how you manage risk while learning.
strongSignals: Structured learning plan (docs, experts, prototypes)
Asked for help early
Managed delivery risk while still learning
Shared what they learned with the team
redFlags: Learned in isolation and delivered late
followUps: Who did you learn from?
What shortcuts did you avoid and why?
What would you teach a newcomer now?

text: Tell me about a time you received critical feedback. How did you respond?
assesses: Openness to feedback and the ability to change behaviour as a result.
strongSignals: Specific feedback, quoted honestly
Listened and asked clarifying questions instead of defending
Visible behaviour change with evidence
Now seeks feedback proactively
followUps: How did you check you had improved?
How do you ask for feedback now?
Have you given similar feedback to others?

text: Tell me about a time you went beyond the stated requirements to solve a customer's real problem.
assesses: Customer obsession: understanding the underlying need and measuring success by customer outcomes.
strongSignals: Talked to customers or used data to find the real need
Balanced customer value against cost and scope
Measured impact after release
Closed the loop with the customer
redFlags: Customer is abstract or absent from the story
followUps: How did you know it was the real problem?
What did you say no to?
What did the metrics show?

text: Describe a live-site incident or outage you were involved in. What was your role, and what happened afterwards?
assesses: Operational ownership of cloud services: calm mitigation, communication and blameless follow-up.
strongSignals: Mitigated first, root-caused later
Clear communication to customers and stakeholders
Blameless postmortem with tracked repair items
Systemic fixes (safe deployment, alerts, automation)
redFlags: Hero narrative with no systemic fix
Did not think about customer impact or communication
followUps: How long until mitigation, and what slowed it?
What repair items did you own?
How did you stop it recurring?

text: Tell me about a project where you needed another team, over which you had no authority, to change their plans to make your project succeed.
assesses: Working across boundaries as One Microsoft: influence without authority and finding shared goals.
strongSignals: Understood the other team's priorities and constraints
Framed the ask around shared outcomes and data
Offered help or compromise
Escalated transparently only when needed
redFlags: Escalated immediately or went around people
No awareness of the other team's incentives
followUps: What did you give up?
How is the relationship now?
What if they had said no?

text: Describe a significant technical disagreement with a peer or senior engineer. How was it resolved?
assesses: Handling conflict constructively, deciding with data and committing to the outcome.
strongSignals: Steelmanned the other view
Used prototypes, data or design reviews to decide
Separated people from the problem
Committed fully once a decision was made
followUps: What if you had been wrong?
What did you learn from their view?
How would you handle it differently?

text: How have you helped include quieter voices or people with different backgrounds in technical decisions on your team?
assesses: Building an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute fully.
strongSignals: Concrete practices (written design reviews, round-robins, async input)
Recognised a specific contribution that would otherwise be missed
Changed team norms, not just one meeting
Reflects on own biases
redFlags: Thinks inclusion is someone else's job
followUps: What changed as a result?
How did you measure it?
What still needs improving?

text: Tell me about a time you mentored or grew another engineer. What was the outcome for them?
assesses: Senior-level multiplier impact through developing others.
strongSignals: Tailored approach to the person's goals
Delegated stretch work with support, not just tasks
Gave candid feedback
Mentee's growth is visible (promotion, ownership, confidence)
redFlags: Mentoring means doing the work for them
Takes credit for the mentee's work
followUps: What did you learn from mentoring them?
How did you handle it when they struggled?
How do you scale mentoring?

text: Tell me about a time you led a project with an ambiguous goal and turned it into a clear technical plan that shipped.
assesses: Turning ambiguity into direction: framing the problem, aligning people and delivering impact.
strongSignals: Clarified the problem and success metrics with stakeholders
Broke the work into milestones that reduced risk
Made and wrote down decisions with explicit trade-offs
Shipped and measured impact
redFlags: Waited for someone else to define it
followUps: What was the hardest decision?
What did you descope?
How did you keep stakeholders aligned?
